reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates transformation toughening by metastable ZrO2 particles in high-entropy carbides, but provides no data or discussion on high-entropy alloys. The hypothesis extrapolates this mechanism to alloys without any cited evidence for alloy-specific behavior, leaving the key premise of transferability unsupported.
premises: In-situ metastable particles can undergo a martensitic-like transformation under mechanical loading in high-entropy alloys.
This transformation generates local compressive stresses and activates crack tip shielding mechanisms (deflection, bridging, branching).
The toughening mechanism observed in high-entropy carbides is transferable to high-entropy alloys.
